decisions.finding: The complete aleph has a shallow horizontal lower-left bar extending beyond its ordinary foot and two comparable rounded right nodes separated by a waist. Literal same-page asher and bracketed vaaherim repeat this compound contour. Neither competing descent appears in the target. The complete contour certifies B2 without expected wording; contact with the ordinary foot does not erase its diagnostic class.

inspections.finding: The full initial vav has a continuous head and shaft with heavy ink at their junction. Literal detached shuruq-vav and vav with a plain midshaft establish the competing anatomy, but an absorbed point cannot be uniquely separated from ordinary head/shaft ink here. Open white area does not prove point absence. Retain the dagesh disclosure.

The kaf lower vowel region is a single broad saturated mass merged into the ordinary bowl. Same-font complete kaf tsere, segol, patah and qamats controls show paired tips, third lower node, shallow plateau and narrow descending stem respectively. The target has insufficient internal or outer contour detail to uniquely exclude coalesced competing classes. Retain without an expected vowel or absence claim.

The complete aleph has a shallow horizontal lower-left bar extending beyond its ordinary foot and two comparable rounded right nodes separated by a waist. Literal same-page asher and bracketed vaaherim repeat this compound contour. The same-page haelohim hataf segol has an additional downward left-class node; the same-font SUS28 mimahorat hataf qamats has a substantial descending left stem/button. Neither competing descent appears in the target. The complete contour certifies B2 without expected wording; contact with the ordinary foot does not erase its diagnostic class.

The nun has a shallow broad lower plateau joined to its ordinary foot across a narrow white slit and small notches. The literal nun patah in SUS38 vaanakhnu and detached het tsere in this unit establish the competing bar and paired classes. The tiny target notches do not uniquely discriminate a ragged bar from a merged horizontal pair; retain.

The complete initial vav ends in a broad solid horizontal base joined to the shaft. Ordinary vav footer, literal under-sheva, qamats, patah and detached tsere controls establish different possible contributions, but the target gives no uniquely bounded lower sign that excludes a fused bar or pair. Retain without expected grammar.

The initial vav within the brackets has a thick shallow solid base with its lower sign merged into the ordinary terminal. Literal same-font foot and point-class controls do not uniquely distinguish bar, fused pair or heavy terminal anatomy. Retain the exact omission and both brackets without an absence claim.
